newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bamerindus sees sale of Inpacel by April.
newsitem.headline: Bamerindus sees sale of Inpacel by April.

text.p: The majority shareholder of Brazil's Bamerindus group said he expects to sell a majority voting stake in pulp and paper maker Inpacel to the Canadian Stern group by April 15, O Estado de Sao Paulo daily said.

Senator Jose Eduardo Andrade Vieira told the newspaper negotiations with the Canadian group advanced after Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), Inpacel's main creditor, agreed to roll over the firm's 205 million real debt with the bank.

O Estado also said Vieira was negotiating with the Central Bank ways to make possible the sale of Bamerindus' 2.3 billion real mortgage portfolio to federal bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF) to solve the bank's liquidity troubles.
According to the newspaper, Vieira rejected the idea of receiving funds from the government's PROER program to promote the restructuring of the banking sector.
Neither the senator nor his aides were available to comment on the report.
Earlier this week, Bamerindus group said it signed a protocol of intentions to sell a stake in Inpacel to the Canadian pulp and paper group.
The protocol is aimed at restructuring Inpacel, whose debt totals 260 million reais, a spokesman for Bamerindus said.
The spokesman confirmed the protocol was presented and approved by the National Development Bank (BNDES).
"The negotiations could not continue without presenting the deal to BNDES," he added.

The restructuring of debt-laden Inpacel would help clean up the finances of Bamerindus bank. For months, the bank has been the object of speculation that it could be sold at any moment due to its widely reported liquidity troubles.

Last year, Bamerindus group announced a restructuring plan under which Bamerindus bank absorbed its profitable Bamerindus Seguros insurance branch, while the bank's expired credits were transferred to its holding company.
Also under the restructuring plan, Inpacel was taken over by Bamerindus Seguros.
But the reorganization of assets was not enough to bail out Bamerindus as so far no money has been injected into the bank.
Based in the southern state of Parana, Bamerindus is among Brazil's 10 largest private banks.
